# Plan business continuity and alternate operations

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

When a disruption could stop critical business activities or key dependencies change. An exercised continuity plan covering owners, alternate operations and a controlled return to normal.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Assess business impacts and dependencies

agent-runnable


List critical customer, payment, workforce and supplier activities and the effects of their loss over time. Record required people, systems, premises, information and counterparties rather than focusing only on servers.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Agree continuity priorities and authority

human · human approval required


Leadership selects tolerable disruption, minimum operating capability, decision owners and escalation routes. Review safety, legal, financial and customer constraints before choosing workarounds.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Prepare alternate operating and communication plans

agent-runnable


Document approved manual or alternate workflows, contact routes, supplier options and restoration dependencies. Protect sensitive information and define which commitments or changes still require separate approval.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Exercise a realistic disruption scenario

human · human approval required


Run a tabletop or approved practical test with the relevant owners and alternates. Capture decisions, unavailable dependencies and customer or staff communication issues without causing an unapproved production interruption.

- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Close gaps and define return-to-normal checks

agent-runnable


Assign fixes and verify that alternate work can be reconciled with restored systems. Record the authority and evidence needed to return to normal and refresh the plan after material business changes.

- Verify: An exercised continuity plan covering owners, alternate operations and a controlled return to normal.
- Sources: [NCSC prepare for incidents](https://www.ncsc.gov.uk/collection/small-business-guidance--response-and-recovery/step-1-prepare-for-incidents) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)
